text_blocks.snippet: A prolapsed bladder, also known as cystocele, can cause a range of symptoms, though some individuals may not experience any noticeable changes. Common symptoms include a feeling of pressure or fullness in the pelvic region, a bulge or lump in the vagina, urinary incontinence (leaking urine), and difficulty emptying the bladder or bowel. Some individuals may also experience pain during sexual intercourse or frequent urinary tract infections.
